source_backed_background.statement: For a nondegenerate braided fusion category, double braiding identifies invertible objects with tensor automorphisms of the identity; in the degenerate case transparent invertibles form the kernel of the same natural map.
For the fully symmetric input Rep(G), Bärenz-Barrett identify their stated Crane-Yetter invariant with a count of flat G-connections.

Ordinary semisimple four-dimensional TFTs, including ordinary Crane-Yetter-Kauffman theories from arbitrary ribbon fusion categories, obey stable-diffeomorphism restrictions and do not detect exotic smooth structure in Reutter's stated scope.
Premodular handle maps retain categorical projection data, including a 3-handle unit-channel projection, before any modular scalar simplification.

fully_symmetric_rep_g.statement: The untwisted Rep(G) special case supplies a calibration target for a future twisted sector construction. It does not prove the general level-1 ansatz.

modular.statement: If the Mueger center is trivial and all level-2 hypotheses hold, the ansatz reduces to the separately recorded modular quadratic-block candidate. That modular formula remains unproved despite 201 matching frozen rows.

simply_connected.statement: For Rep(G), pi1=1 leaves one flat homomorphism. For arbitrary premodular C, this note makes no general sector-collapse assertion. Even a one-sector reduction would not prove quadratic alpha-dependence.
